item.title: [2456] Nov. 22, 2026: American Oversight v. ICE, DOD, and USSC — Order
[38956] 2026-11 - A-2026-35897 - Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada
item.description: I am writing to request records under the Access to Information Act relating to the Start-Up Visa (SUV) Program, for the period January 1, 2020 to the 2026-07-24. To ensure clarity and facilitate processing, I have attached a spreadsheet template illustrating the structure and data fields requested. The spreadsheet is provided as a guide only and reflects the categories described below. Purpose of Year-of-Filing Comparison This request seeks a year-by-year breakdown to permit comparison among applications filed in the same calendar year. In particular, the requested data will identify, for each designated organization and for each filing year, how many Start-Up Visa applications from that cohort have received a final decision (approval or refusal) and how many remain undecided. This information is requested to assess whether applications from the same filing cohort have generally been processed while others remain outstanding. Scope of Request For all Start-Up Visa permanent residence applications, broken down by designated organization, please provide the following information: 1. Applications Received Total number of Start-Up Visa applications received by IRCC Shown: by calendar year (2020 onward), and cumulatively Broken down by designated organization 2. Applications In Process (No Final Decision) Number of applications currently in process with no final decision Including: applications with an assigned GCMS file number, and applications received but not yet assigned a file number, if tracked Shown: by calendar year of receipt, and cumulatively Broken down by designated organization 3. Applications Finalized Decisions Rendered For applications with a final decision: Number of approved applications Number of refused applications Shown: by calendar year of decision, and cumulatively Broken down by designated organization 4. Definitions / Notes Any internal definitions used for: application received in process approved refused Any known limitations or qualifications affecting the data (e.g., delays between receipt and GCMS file creation) If any portion of this request is unclear or overly broad, I would appreciate the opportunity to clarify or refine it. (From: 2020-01-01 To: 2026-07-24). | 154 pages | Source: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada

item.title: [38956] 2026-11 - A-2025-73417 - Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada
item.description: I am requesting access to final copies of internal records held by the IRCC Access to Information and Privacy (ATIP) Division that describe or explain how IRCC manages Access to Information Act and Privacy Act requests that are completed beyond the statutory 30-day timeframe without a formal time extension notice issued under section 9 of the Access to Information Act or subsection 15(1) of the Privacy Act. This request focuses specifically on statutory time management, implied extensions, and procedural compliance. The records I am seeking include, but are not limited to: [1] Internal policies, procedures, directives, manuals, or memoranda describing how IRCC handles cases where ATIP responses exceed 30 days without a formal time extension notice. [2] Records or internal communications outlining any automated or manual scheduling mechanisms, backlog queues, or systematic approaches that result in completion intervals of approximately 30, 60, 90, 120, or 180 days beyond the statutory deadline. [3] Reports, audits, or analyses assessing IRCC's compliance with section 9 of the Access to Information Act and subsection 15(1) of the Privacy Act, particularly regarding instances where time extensions were implied but not formally communicated. [4] Instructions, guidance, or notes distributed to ATIP officers or management that address how to manage, track, or categorize requests once the statutory period has expired without a formal extension notice. Clarification: This request concerns the processes, practices, or internal rationale by which IRCC completes Access to Information Act and Privacy Act requests late without issuing time extension notices, and related internal rules, workflows, or decision criteria used in such circumstances. Additional Information: A separate one-page document is attached to illustrate the nature of delayed ATIP responses and the observed pattern of implied extensions. Time period: January 1, 2024 to October 17, 2025. | 19 pages | Source: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada

item.title: [30736] Dutch Prime Minister's Office — Woo Decision on Jared Kushner Financial Intelligence Briefings (2018)
item.description: On November 4, 2026, the Netherlands Ministry of General Affairs issued a formal decision under the Dutch Open Government Act (Wet open overheid) concerning a request for records establishing whether the Dutch Prime Minister or his office received briefings in 2018 about alleged financial transactions involving Jared Kushner, First Abu Dhabi Bank, and financial institutions in Azerbaijan, Israel, and Cyprus. The ministry reported searching its document management system using multiple names and keywords and consulting relevant personnel. It concluded that no responsive documents were located and denied the request on that basis. The decision identifies the ministry's search methodology and provides instructions for filing an administrative objection. | 2 pages | Source: William Fernandes
